label: Germany — Technical Recession
sub: Europe's largest economy entered technical recession in 2024–2025, hit by energy costs from Russia sanctions, weak Chinese demand for exports, and US tariff exposure. GDP contracted two consecutive quarters; manufacturing PMI persistently in contraction.

label: United Kingdom — Stagnation Risk
sub: UK GDP contracted 0.1% in Q4 2024, narrowly avoiding technical recession. CPI projected to peak at 4% in Sep 2025; Bank Rate cut 6 times to 3.75% since Aug 2024. Consumer confidence weak as cost-of-living squeeze persists.

label: Argentina — 220% Inflation Crisis
sub: Argentina suffered 220% annual inflation in 2024, the highest in the world among major economies. President Milei's 'chainsaw' austerity program slashed government spending and deregulated the economy. GDP contracted sharply before beginning stabilization under IMF program.

label: Turkey — Rate Shock Stabilization
sub: Turkey shifted to monetary orthodoxy in 2023–2024, raising rates dramatically from ~8% to 40%+ to combat chronic inflation. The lira lost significant value against the dollar. The rate shock caused a severe economic slowdown before inflation began to moderate.

label: Sri Lanka — Post-Default IMF Recovery
sub: Sri Lanka defaulted on its sovereign debt in 2022 and began an IMF restructuring program. By 2025, the economy was in fragile recovery mode with significant debt service obligations and tight IMF conditionality constraining growth and social spending.

label: Egypt — IMF Bailout & Currency Crisis
sub: Egypt faced a severe foreign currency crisis in 2024, with the Egyptian pound losing more than half its value against the dollar. Inflation exceeded 30% at peak. The IMF expanded its support program to stabilize the economy. Tourism revenues and Suez Canal income provided some relief.

label: Nigeria — Naira Devaluation Shock
sub: Nigeria devalued the naira in 2023–2024 as part of IMF-backed reforms, leading to sharp inflation above 25% and severe cost-of-living crisis. Oil revenue volatility and fuel subsidy removal compounded economic pressures, contributing to rising recession risk.

label: Pakistan — IMF Bailout & Debt Stress
sub: Pakistan secured a $3B+ IMF Stand-By Arrangement in 2023 and extended program in 2024–2025, averting sovereign default. Foreign reserves had fallen to critical levels. The economy faces high debt-to-GDP, chronic inflation, and structural fiscal deficits requiring continued external support.

label: Washington DC — 'Big Beautiful Bill' Adds $3T+ to US Debt; Bond Vigilantes Drive 30Y Near 5.09% (May 23)
sub: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 2025): +$2.4T primary deficits, +$3.0T with interest over 10 years, up to $5T if provisions extended. Debt ceiling raised $5T. CBO: +0.9pp GDP boost but unsustainable fiscal trajectory. Fortune (May 23): 'US debt is the elephant in the room' in bond selloff. Moody's Aa1 downgrade (May 16) + Big Beautiful Bill + Warsh $6.7T QT plans = structurally elevated yields. 30Y at ~5.09% (near 5.189% 18-yr high). Citi targets 5.5%; BofA 62% expect 6%. 30Y mortgage: ~7.5-7.6%. Section 122 cliff July 23 (60 days). S&P 500 8 consecutive weekly gains (7,473.47 close May 22).

label: White House — Warsh Sworn In as 17th Fed Chair (May 22); First WH Ceremony Since Greenspan 1987
sub: Kevin Warsh formally sworn in at White House at 11 a.m. EDT on May 22, 2026 — the first Fed Chair swearing-in ceremony at the White House since Alan Greenspan was sworn in in 1987. Warsh confirmed 54-45 Senate May 13. He inherits: CPI 3.8%, PPI 6.0%, Core PCE 3.2% — all above 2% target; FOMC April minutes showing rate hike discussion; 30Y Treasury ~5.09% (near 18-yr highs); Flash PMI Composite 51.7 implying Q2 GDP ~1%. First FOMC as Chair: June 16-17 (SEP + dot plot + press conference). Section 122 cliff July 23 (62 days).

label: Washington DC — Warsh Fed Era; FOMC Minutes Hawkish Pivot
sub: Kevin Warsh assumed Federal Reserve Chair May 15, 2026 (Day 1). FOMC April 28-29 minutes (released May 20) showed officials explicitly discussed rate hikes — Hammack, Kashkari, Logan opposed easing bias; 30Y Treasury at 5.18-5.20% (18-year high). Fed Governor Barr publicly opposed Warsh's $6.7T QT plans (Axios, May 20). First Warsh FOMC: June 16-17 with new SEP. Section 122 tariff cliff July 23.

label: Beijing — China Tariff Retaliation Hub
sub: China faced US tariffs of up to 145% in April 2025 before a temporary truce reduced them to ~30%. China retaliated with 84% tariffs on US goods. The PBOC eased monetary policy aggressively to counteract deflationary pressures from the property crisis and trade war.

label: Ottawa — Canada Retaliates Against US Tariffs
sub: Canada was hit with 25% US tariffs in February–March 2025, citing fentanyl and border security. Ottawa announced C$30 billion in retaliatory tariffs on US goods. The Bank of Canada cut interest rates aggressively to cushion the economic blow, particularly to the auto and agricultural sectors.

label: Mexico City — US Tariffs Hit Near-Shoring Boom
sub: Mexico faced 25% US tariffs under IEEPA in early 2025. The country had benefited from 'near-shoring' trends as companies relocated supply chains from China, but tariff threats created new uncertainty. The peso experienced sharp volatility and Pemex's fiscal burden complicated the response.

label: Brussels — EU-US Tariff Negotiations
sub: The EU faced 20% tariffs under Trump's Liberation Day reciprocal tariff scheme (paused for 90 days). European Commission and ECB officials warned of severe growth impacts, particularly for German auto exports. The ECB cut rates eight times to 2.00% partly in response to trade-war headwinds.

label: Frankfurt — ECB June 11 Hike at 99% Probability: Deposit Rate to 2.25% (First Hike Since July 2023); Eurozone CPI 3.0%
sub: ECB cut rates eight times (Jun 2024 → Jun 2025) to 2.00%. Apr 30 hold: Held as Eurozone CPI flash hit 3.0% (Iran war energy shock). JUNE 11 DECISION (4 DAYS): Markets price 99% probability of 25bp hike to 2.25% deposit rate — the first ECB rate increase since July 2023 and a full reversal of the easing trajectory. ECB hawks (Schnabel, Holzmann) cited persistent services inflation and second-round wage effects. Lagarde signaled 'new assessment' at June 11. At least 1 additional hike priced by year-end 2026. Germany (technical recession) is the most exposed eurozone economy to ECB tightening; Italy BTP-Bund spread is the key stress indicator.

label: London — Bank of England Rate Cuts
sub: The Bank of England cut its policy rate six times since August 2024, reducing it from 5.25% to 3.75% by early 2026. The MPC navigated the difficult trade-off of weak UK growth against above-target inflation (CPI above 2% target). Governor Andrew Bailey emphasized a gradual approach.

label: Tokyo — BOJ June 16 Hike at 96%+ Probability (to 1.00%); Simultaneous with Warsh FOMC Day 1 — August 2024 Carry Unwind Replay Risk Elevated
sub: Bloomberg June 4: BOJ mulling 25bp hike to 1.00% at June 15-16 meeting — highest Japanese policy rate since 2008. CME: 96%+ market probability for June hike. Drivers: core CPI persistently above 2%; Iran war energy shock adds 0.3-0.5pp to Japan inflation; hawkish internal BOJ split (Apr 28: 3 dissenters pushed for immediate 1.00%). FY2026 GDP forecast: 0.5%; core CPI: 2.8%. CRITICAL OVERLAP: BOJ June 16 decision (Japan morning) coincides EXACTLY with Warsh inaugural FOMC June 16-17 Day 1. If BOJ hikes + Warsh June 17 dot plot signals December hike = August 2024 'Black Monday II' replay (Nikkei -12%, VIX 65, Nasdaq -3.4%, estimated $4T yen carry trades unwinding). JGB 10Y: ~2.11%.

label: Vietnam — Key Manufacturing Hub Hit by Reciprocal Tariffs
sub: Vietnam was one of the highest-tariffed countries under Trump's Liberation Day tariffs (46% reciprocal rate), targeting its large electronics and textile export sector. As a key alternative manufacturing hub to China, tariff disruption threatened to reverse near-shoring trends that had been driving Vietnam's rapid growth.

label: Seoul — Political Crisis Compounds Trade Risk
sub: South Korea faced both political crisis (President Yoon's martial law attempt, impeachment, and arrest in December 2024) and US tariff risk on its semiconductor and auto exports. The Bank of Korea cut rates to buffer the economic impact, while political instability added investor uncertainty.

label: Rome — Italy BTP-Bund Spread Under Watch
sub: Italy's BTP-Bund yield spread remained a key eurozone stress indicator. With debt-to-GDP near 140%, Italy is dependent on the ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI) backstop and low borrowing costs. Any ECB policy miscalibration or political crisis could reignite Italian sovereign debt stress.

label: Paris — France Fiscal Deficit Above EU Limits
sub: France's fiscal deficit exceeded 6% of GDP in 2024–2025, well above the EU's 3% ceiling, prompting EU excessive deficit procedure. Political instability following snap elections weakened the government's ability to enact consolidation. French bond spreads widened against German Bunds as fiscal concerns mounted.

label: Shenzhen/Pearl River Delta — China Property Crisis Epicenter
sub: Southern China's property and finance hub, home to Evergrande's headquarters and major developer defaults. The collapse of property giant Evergrande (liquidation ordered January 2024) and Country Garden's default exposed trillions in local government financing vehicle (LGFV) debt. The property sector had accounted for ~25% of China's GDP.

label: Brazil — High Real Interest Rates & Debt Costs
sub: Brazil maintained the Selic rate among the world's highest real interest rates in 2024–2025. High domestic borrowing costs increased debt service burden on the government. Brazil's fiscal deficit expansion fueled concerns about debt sustainability and limited the central bank's room to cut rates to support growth.

label: Sub-Saharan Africa — Debt Refinancing Stress
sub: Multiple Sub-Saharan African economies — including Ghana, Zambia, Ethiopia, and Kenya — faced acute sovereign debt stress in 2024–2025 as dollar debt matured at high interest rates. Several countries sought IMF support programs. Zambia completed an historic restructuring in 2023, setting a precedent for others.

label: New Delhi — India: Tariff Risk vs China Decoupling Benefit
sub: India benefited from US-China decoupling as manufacturing shifted toward India (Apple iPhone production, etc.), but faces its own tariff exposure under Trump's reciprocal tariff scheme. South Asia growth projected at 6.2% for 2026 per World Bank. India's relatively closed economy offers some buffer against global trade slowdown.

label: Beirut — Bank Deposits Frozen, Reconstruction Debt
sub: Lebanon's financial system remained in severe crisis through 2025–2026, with bank deposits frozen since 2019 and no viable restructuring agreement. Post-war reconstruction financing (following 2024 conflict) added to an already unsustainable debt load. The IMF and World Bank were engaged but a reform program remained elusive.

label: Zambia — Post-Default Debt Restructuring Precedent
sub: Zambia completed its landmark sovereign debt restructuring in 2023 — the first African country to restructure under the G20 Common Framework. The successful completion was closely watched as a template for other distressed African debtors (Ethiopia, Ghana) while Zambia itself faces a fragile stabilization period through 2025–2026.

label: US Midwest/Labor — ISM Mfg 54.0% (June 1) + JOLTS 7.6M Openings (June 2) + May Jobs Report June 5 — Labor Demand Resilient
sub: Chicago PMI surged to 62.7 (May 29) — 4-year high, biggest monthly jump since 2020. ISM Manufacturing PMI May 2026 (June 1): 54.0% (5th consecutive expansion month; New Orders 56.8%; corresponds to 2.2% annualized GDP growth; strongest since May 2022). BLS JOLTS April 2026 (June 2): job openings rose to 7.6M (from 6.9M revised March) — significant beat; hires slowed to 5.1M; layoffs stable 1.7M; Sahm Rule ~0.43% (below 0.5% threshold). May payrolls report (BLS June 5) is the next critical labor market test. Three consecutive PMI beats + JOLTS beat = manufacturing + labor demand intact despite tariff/Iran war headwinds.

label: Shanghai — NBS PMI 50.0 (Borderline, May 31) + Caixin PMI 51.8% (June 1 Beat); SME/Private Sector Diverges From State Sector
sub: NBS Manufacturing PMI (May 31): 50.0 borderline; new orders 49.9 (contraction — first below 50 in 3 months); tracks large SOEs/export sector. Caixin Manufacturing PMI May 2026 (June 1): 51.8% (beat 51.4% consensus; down from 52.2% April); tracks SME/private sector — domestic demand, new customers, product upgrades drive activity; export orders dipped; input/output prices eased first time in 7 months. DIVERGENCE: NBS 50.0 (SOEs stalling) vs. Caixin 51.8% (private sector expanding). Q1 GDP: 5.0% (front-loaded). Q2 momentum decelerating. PBOC RRR cut likely. US-China effective tariff: ~31.6%.

label: Singapore — Asian Trade Bellwether Under Pressure
sub: Singapore's open economy serves as a real-time indicator of Asia-Pacific trade flows. The city-state's electronics exports and container throughput declined materially in tariff-disruption periods. Singapore's central bank (MAS) maintained exchange rate-based policy accommodation to support exports during the global trade war.

label: Amsterdam/Rotterdam — European Trade Gateway at Risk
sub: The Port of Rotterdam, Europe's largest, serves as a key gateway for US and Asian goods to Europe. Under the Liberation Day tariff regime, major re-routing of trade flows was anticipated. The Netherlands' highly open export-dependent economy made it among the most exposed European economies to US tariff disruption.

label: Beijing — Trump-Xi Summit (Apr 1–2, 2026)
sub: President Trump's first visit to China since 2017 (March 31–April 2, 2026) focused on agriculture purchases, rare earth export control concessions (China controls ~69% of global rare earth supply), and fentanyl enforcement. Analysts expected a process not a breakthrough. China's trade surplus hit a record $213.6 billion in Jan–Feb 2026 and exports surged 21.8% YoY, giving Beijing leverage. Section 232 auto tariffs (25%) remained off the table.

label: Beijing — Trump-Xi Summit COMPLETE (May 14-15): 'Meagre' Outcomes — Boeing 200 Jets, Ag Pledge, Partial Rare Earth Truce; No Iran/H200 Deal
sub: Two-day summit (May 14-15) at Great Hall of the People. Framework: 'constructive, strategic and stable' bilateral relationship for 3+ years. Xi called it 'landmark'; analysts called it 'meagre.' Day 2 deliverables: Boeing 200-jet order (vs 500 expected — Boeing -4%); agriculture 'double-digit billions' (unspecified); China buys US oil; rare earth mutual de-escalation (Trump dropped 100% tariff threat; China paused export restrictions — NOT a formal deal); Board of Trade ~$30B tariff reduction (framework only). KEY GAPS: No Iran/Hormuz cooperation — Sec. Rubio said Trump 'did not ask Xi for help'; no H200 Nvidia definitive chip deal. Follow-up: Trump invited Xi to Washington September; two more face-to-faces. S&P 500 -0.9% on May 15 summit disappointment. Section 122 cliff July 23 (68 days).

label: Washington DC — Supreme Court IEEPA Ruling
sub: On February 20, 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that IEEPA does not authorize the executive to impose tariffs, striking down most of the 2025 tariff regime. Markets rallied. The administration responded four days later by invoking Section 122 of the Trade Act to reimpose a 10% tariff on $1.2 trillion of imports for 150 days.

label: Strasbourg — EU Parliament Backs Turnberry Trade Deal 417–154
sub: On March 26, 2026, the European Parliament voted 417-154 to advance the 'Turnberry' EU-US trade framework, which would set a 15% US tariff on EU exports (down from 20% Liberation Day rate) in exchange for EU market opening. A sunset clause (expires Mar 2028) and sunrise clause (conditional on US compliance) were attached. Final ratification requires EU Council approval.

label: Washington DC — Liberation Day Anniversary Tariff Expansion (Apr 2, 2026)
sub: One year after Liberation Day, Trump expanded Section 232 metal tariffs (50% on steel/aluminum/copper articles, 25% on derivatives) and announced 100% tariffs on patented pharmaceuticals (effective 120–180 days). The announcement triggered a historic $6.6 trillion two-day market crash (S&P -10%, Nasdaq bear market). The tariff expansion covers approximately $400B in additional import value.

label: Beijing — China Tariff Escalation: 84% on All US Goods (Apr 9, 2026)
sub: April 4: China announced 34% blanket tariff on all US imports (effective Apr 10), triggering worst crash day (S&P -5.97%). April 9: China raised tariffs to 84% in response to Trump's additional 50% (US now at ~104% on China). China vowed to 'fight to the end.' Combined bilateral tariff barrier approaches near-embargo levels not seen since 1930s.

label: Muscat, Oman — Muscat Protocol + US-Iran Ceasefire (Apr 5–7, 2026)
sub: April 5: Iran-Oman 'Muscat Protocol' opened 'Green Channel' for Hormuz commercial shipping, relieving the worst supply shock. April 7: Full US-Iran two-week ceasefire announced, sending WTI crashing 16.4% to $94.41 (biggest single-day oil decline since Apr 2020) and Dow surging 1,325 points (+2.85%). Ceasefire is fragile — Lebanon strikes continue, Iran and US proposals conflict on key terms.

label: Washington DC — US Imposes 104% Tariff on China (Apr 9, 2026)
sub: On April 9, 2026, Trump followed through on his ultimatum and imposed an additional 50% tariff on all Chinese imports, bringing the effective US tariff rate on Chinese goods to ~104% — the highest since the 1930s Smoot-Hawley era. China responded with 84% tariffs on US goods. The dual tariff shock pushed JPMorgan recession probability to 65% and Moody's Analytics to ~50%.

label: IMF — Global Inflation Crisis Warning
sub: IMF warned April 9 of a looming global inflation crisis driven by the US-Israel war on Iran. The Fund's assessment adds a major multilateral institution's voice to stagflation risk signals from JPMorgan, Moody's Analytics, and Goldman Sachs.

label: Washington DC — IMF Spring Meetings Apr 13–18, 2026 (Concluded)
sub: IMF–World Bank Spring Meetings concluded April 18. WEO April 2026 (released Apr 14) confirmed global growth at 3.1% (reference), 2.5% (adverse), 2.0% (severe). Headline inflation 4.4% globally. Mid-East & Central Asia slashed 2pp to 1.9%. IMF pledged $20-50B emergency support for energy-importing EMDEs. G-24 demanded accelerated quota reform. Powell's Fed Chair term (expires May 15) and ECB rate hike re-pricing dominated the macro agenda alongside FOMC April 29-30.

label: Beijing — China Q1 2026 GDP: 5.0% (Beat); March Exports Slump
sub: China NBS reported Q1 2026 GDP of 5.0% year-over-year (beat: forecast 4.8%), accelerating from 4.5% in Q4 2025 — driven by Jan-Feb export surge (+21.8% YoY). However, March exports slowed sharply to +2.5% YoY (miss vs +8.6% forecast) as Iran war dampened Middle East demand. Factory-gate PPI turned positive (+0.5%) for first time in 3+ years — reversing China's deflationary trend. Canton Fair order data for Q2 signals continued export weakness.

label: Washington DC — CAPE Portal: $166B IEEPA Tariff Refunds Launched (Apr 20, 2026)
sub: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) launched the CAPE (Customs Automated Protest and Entry) portal on April 20, 2026, enabling US importers to claim refunds on ~$166 billion in IEEPA tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court (Feb 20, 2026). System experienced high-volume crashes on Day 1; 56,000+ importers in queue. Effective tariff rate remains 8.9% overall (31.6% China) under surviving Section 122 authority. The $166B liability is ~6.4% of annual federal revenues — one of the largest customs refund events in US history.

label: Washington DC — BofA: No Fed Cuts Until July 2027; Goldman 30% Recession; Moody's 49%; 10Y Yield 4.59% (May 16)
sub: May 16, 2026: Bank of America withdrew all 2026 rate cut forecasts — first cut pushed to July 2027, second September 2027. BofA traders now price >50% probability of at least one rate hike by March 2027. Goldman Sachs raised US recession probability to 30% (from ~20%). Moody's Analytics at 49% (approaching 50% threshold). 10Y Treasury weekly close: 4.59% — highest since May 2025. Warsh assumes Fed Chair May 15. Next FOMC: June 16-17, 2026. Section 122 tariff cliff: July 23, 2026 (67 days).

label: Washington DC — CIT Declares Section 122 Tariffs Unlawful (May 7); Federal Circuit Stay (May 12) — Tariffs Still Active
sub: May 7, 2026: US Court of International Trade ruled 2-1 that Proclamation 11012 (Section 122 tariffs) was unlawful — finding 'trade and current account deficits do not constitute a balance-of-payments deficit within the meaning of Section 122' of the Trade Act of 1974. Scope: limited to plaintiff importers only (Burlap & Barrel, Basic Fun, State of Washington). May 12: US Court of Appeals (Federal Circuit) issued administrative stay — Section 122 tariffs still collected by all importers pending appeal. USTR Greer (May 17): US can restore 'Busan Deal' ~41.6% China rate under alternative authorities if Section 122 ultimately struck down. Section 122 cliff July 23 (66 days) remains primary deadline regardless of court outcome.

label: New York — Moody's Downgrades US Aaa→Aa1 (May 16) + Fannie/Freddie Aa1 (May 19)
sub: May 16, 2026 (after close): Moody's downgraded the United States from Aaa to Aa1 — first time all three agencies (S&P 2011, Fitch 2023, Moody's 2026) simultaneously below top tier. May 19: Moody's follows with Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac Aa1 downgrade — GSE MBS spreads widen; 30-year mortgage rates approaching 7.6%. May 19 bond market reaction: 30Y Treasury hit 5.189% (highest since July 2007). Citi targets 5.5% as next level. BofA survey: 62% expect 30Y to reach 6%.

label: Washington DC — 30Y Treasury Hits 5.189% (May 19 — 19-Year High); Citi Eyes 5.5%; BofA Survey 62% Expect 6%
sub: May 19, 2026 (Day 5 of Warsh era): US 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.189% — the highest since July 2007 (19 years). Citi flagged 5.5% as next key level (last seen ~22 years ago). BofA fund manager survey: 62% expect 30Y to hit 6% — highest such expectation since 1999. Drivers: Moody's Aa1 sovereign downgrade (May 16); Warsh $6.7T QT plans increasing Treasury supply; CPI 3.8%/PPI 6.0% inflation. S&P 500 -0.55% (~7,372); Gold >$3,200. Section 122 cliff July 23 (64 days). FOMC June 16-17 (Warsh's first SEP + press conference).

label: New York — S&P 500 –2.6% to 7,383.74 (June 5 — Worst Day Since Oct 2025); Goldman Cuts Recession to 15%; Triple CB Week June 11-17
sub: June 5: S&P 500 fell 200.57 pts (–2.6%) to 7,383.74 — worst single-day decline since October 2025. Nasdaq –4.2% to 25,709.43. Trigger: May NFP +172K blowout → December 2026 rate hike fully priced. 10Y yield 4.544%; 2Y 4.162% (2026 high). June 6 weekend: Goldman Sachs formally cut US recession probability to 15% (from 25%) — 'no landing' now base case. 'Paycheck recession' concurrent warning: real income eroding at pace rarely seen outside recessions. Critical week: ECB June 11 (99% 25bp hike to 2.25%), BOJ June 16 (96%+ 25bp hike to 1.00%), Warsh FOMC June 16-17 (dot plot).

label: Gulf — Iran MOU Unsigned Day 7 (June 5); Brent ~$97; Trump Edits Draft; VP Vance: Signing 'Uncertain'
sub: Iran MOU unsigned on Day 7 (June 5) as Trump returned draft to negotiators demanding stronger language on nuclear commitments: clearer enrichment suspension timelines, disposition of Iran's 440+ kg of 60%-enriched uranium stockpile, immediate Hormuz handover on signing. VP Vance: 'Hard to say exactly when or if the president's going to sign.' Brent fell from ~$101 (June 3) to ~$97 (June 5) on continued deal optimism despite no signature. IEA floor: ~$80-82 even with full reopening. Goldman: signed deal + Brent $88 = recession probability from ~25% toward 18%. Next window: June 9-17 (before Warsh FOMC).

label: New York — S&P 500 Record 7,519.12 (May 26); Nasdaq Record 26,656; Micron +19% AI Surge; Sentiment/Equity Divergence Historic
sub: May 26 (Memorial Day reopening): S&P 500 hit new record close 7,519.12 (+0.61%); Nasdaq record 26,656.18 (+1.19%); Dow 50,461.68 (-0.23%). Catalyst: Micron +19% after UBS upgrade, crossing $1T market cap — AI semiconductor complex rally. 9th consecutive week of gains. S&P at all-time high while Michigan Consumer Sentiment at 70-year record low (44.8) — the widest sentiment/equity divergence in market history. 10Y Treasury fell 8 bps to 4.489%; 30Y to 5.024% on Iran peace optimism. CB Consumer Confidence May: 93.1 (beat; but 16th month Expectations below 80 recession threshold).

label: Washington DC — April PCE 3.3% Core / 3.8% Headline (3-Year Highs); Q1 GDP Revised Down to +1.6%; S&P 500 New ATH ~7,557 (May 28)
sub: BEA May 28 triple release: (1) April PCE: headline 3.8% YoY (3-year high), core 3.3% YoY (3-year high), BUT MoM softer (core +0.2% vs +0.3% feared) — supercore decelerated to +0.1%. Real disposable income -0.5% (2nd consecutive monthly decline); saving rate 2.6% multi-year low. (2) Q1 2026 GDP 2nd estimate: +1.6% (revised from +2.0%); consumer spending + residential investment revised lower. (3) Durable Goods April: +7.9% MoM (largely aircraft orders). June FOMC hold ~99% priced. S&P 500 new ATH ~7,557 on 'less bad than feared' PCE MoM — Snowflake +36.5%.

label: Washington DC — Warsh $6.7T Balance Sheet Reduction Signal (May 17); Could Push 10Y Yield Above 4.59%
sub: May 17, 2026 (Day 3 of Warsh chairmanship): Multiple analyses report Warsh intends to aggressively reduce the $6.7 trillion Fed balance sheet (vs pre-2008 baseline of ~$900B), arguing it 'disproportionately helps those with financial assets' and distorts markets. If successful: 10Y yield could rise above 4.59% weekly close toward 5.00%+; Shiller CAPE ~38.6 would face additional compression pressure; corporate/mortgage borrowing costs would rise. First FOMC signal: June 16-17, 2026. Balance sheet trajectory (QT resumption/acceleration) is the most consequential policy question of the Warsh era beyond the rate decision.

label: Washington DC — Warsh Senate Floor Vote May 11-12 (~92%); Powell Expires May 15; S&P 500 at 7,398
sub: Apr 29: Warsh cleared Senate Banking 13-11 (historic party-line vote). May 8: BLS April jobs +115K beat — Warsh inherits labor market resilience + PCE 3.2% core stagflation. May 9: Senate floor vote expected May 11-12; Sen. Fetterman (D-PA) signaled yes vote. Prediction markets: ~92% confirmation. Warsh chairs June FOMC (June 9-10) against backdrop: S&P 500 ATH 7,398.93 (six-week streak), oil ~$101 Brent (still elevated), ISM Services Prices Paid 70.7. Market risk: Warsh balance-sheet reduction stance could push long yields higher than Powell's approach. July 23 Section 122 tariff cliff (75 days) will be his first major policy challenge.

label: Washington DC — BEA Q1 2026 GDP +2.0% Advance; March PCE 3.5%/3.2% Core (Apr 30, 2026)
sub: April 30, 2026: BEA released Q1 2026 GDP advance (+2.0% annualized — beat GDPNow 1.2%) and March PCE simultaneously. Headline PCE: 3.5% YoY (+0.7% MoM); Core PCE: 3.2% YoY (+0.3% MoM) — hottest since Iran war began. GDP beat reduces recession probability; hot PCE confirms stagflation trap. Goldman: ~25%, JPMorgan: ~30%, Moody's: ~42%.

label: Islamabad — Iran FM Araghchi Peace Talks (Apr 24, 2026)
sub: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi flew to Islamabad on April 24, 2026 for indirect US-Iran peace negotiations facilitated by Pakistan. The diplomacy followed Iran's IRGC ship seizures in the Strait of Hormuz on April 23. Pakistan serves as a back-channel mediator. Araghchi was scheduled to travel onward to Oman (Muscat) and Moscow. Trump declined a timeline ('Don't rush me'). US Defense Secretary Hegseth declared a full naval blockade of Hormuz, with an additional carrier deploying.

label: Strait of Hormuz — 'Project Freedom' Military Escort Launches May 4; Shipping at 9% of Normal
sub: May 4: Trump launches 'Project Freedom' — US military escort for commercial vessels through Hormuz (guided-missile destroyers, 100+ aircraft, 15,000 personnel). Iran calls it a ceasefire violation; IRGC claims Strait control. Disputed missile attack report (Fars: 2 missiles hit US warship; US Navy denies). Shipping volume: ~12 crossings/day vs 129/day pre-war (9%). Brent $115/WTI $103.42. EIA: 10.1 mbpd disrupted — largest oil supply shock since 1973 Arab embargo. Iran 14-point ceasefire counter-proposal submitted May 2.

label: Washington DC — EU 25% Auto Tariffs Effective May 5; Section 301 Hearing (16 Countries); Section 122 Cliff July 23
sub: May 5: Trump's 25% auto tariffs on EU cars/light trucks take effect (~$70-80B/year in trade). USTR Section 301 public hearings (May 5-8) target 16 countries (EU, China, Japan, India, Vietnam, South Korea, Taiwan, Mexico, etc.) — next tariff wave previewed with aim to conclude before July 23 Section 122 cliff. CRITICAL DEADLINE: Section 122 tariffs expire July 23, 2026 (150-day limit) — Congressional action required. Section 301 investigations likely provide alternative legal basis post-July.

label: Sydney — RBA Hikes +25 bps to 4.35% (May 2026); Third Consecutive 2026 Rate Increase
sub: Reserve Bank of Australia raised cash rate to 4.35% in May 2026 — third consecutive hike in 2026 (also hiked Feb and Mar), reversing all 2025 cuts. 8-1 board vote. Australia CPI: 4.6% YoY (March 2026) driven by Iran war energy shock and second-round effects across utilities and freight. Governor Bullock: 'Will do what is necessary.' Westpac forecasts two more hikes (June, August) to 4.85%. RBA is the only G7+ central bank actively tightening as of May 2026.

label: Strait of Hormuz — Iran Strikes Korean Vessel (May 5); Oil Crashes on Ceasefire Progress (May 6); Brent ~$100 (May 7-8)
sub: May 5: Iran's IRGC seized/disabled a South Korean VLCC tanker in Hormuz — Brent surged to ~$114; Dow fell 1.1%. May 6: Trump paused 'Project Freedom'; Iran submitted revised ceasefire proposal via Pakistan — Brent crashed 8-9% to $103. May 7-8: Oil continued easing to ~$100-101 Brent / $91 WTI as ceasefire talks advanced and BLS April jobs report (+115K beat) reduced economic pessimism. 14-point US-Iran MOU under Iranian review.

label: Washington DC — BLS April 2026 Jobs: +115K (Beat); Unemployment 4.3%; Warsh Vote 3 Days Away
sub: May 8, 2026: BLS released April Employment Situation — +115,000 nonfarm payrolls (strong beat vs ~60K consensus). Unemployment rate 4.3% (unchanged). February revised to –156,000 (deepest monthly loss since April 2020). March revised to +185,000. Sector gains: health care +37K, transportation +30K, retail +22K. Federal government –9K (DOGE cuts). Recession probabilities eased: Goldman ~20%, JPMorgan ~25%, Moody's ~40%. S&P 500 rallied to ~7,395 on the beat. Kevin Warsh Senate floor vote expected May 11-12 (3 days).

label: Seoul — Bessent-He Lifeng Trade Talks Day 1: 'Very Good'; Tariff Stability Maintained (May 12, 2026)
sub: Day 1 (May 12): Bessent told CNBC talks were 'very good' — both sides agreed to 'continue to maintain the stability of tariffs.' Focus on Chinese purchase commitments and bilateral investment mechanism. No new tariff changes in either direction. China opposed Section 301 investigations. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung held side meeting with Bessent on South Korean tariff exposure. Day 2 (May 13) with USTR Greer/Li Chenggang. Feeds into Trump-Xi Beijing summit May 14-15. Board of Trade managed-trade mechanism remains most likely institutional outcome.

label: Washington DC — Warsh Senate Governor Confirmation May 12; Chair Vote Imminent (May 13); April CPI 3.8% Hot Print
sub: May 11: Senate voted 49-44 cloture (Fetterman + Coons crossed). May 12: Senate confirmed Warsh as Fed GOVERNOR (14-year term) — first of two required votes. Chair vote expected May 13 (Powell expires May 15). APRIL CPI RELEASED May 12: 3.8% YoY (highest since May 2023), core +0.4% MoM (highest since Jan 2025), energy +17.9% YoY. CME FedWatch raised rate HIKE probability to ~30% by year-end. S&P 500 fell ~0.4% on hot CPI. Warsh era begins with rising hike pressure — June 9-10 FOMC will be first test.

label: Washington DC — BLS April 2026 CPI: 3.8% YoY — Hot Print; Core +0.4% MoM; CME Hike Odds Rise to ~30%
sub: BLS released April 2026 CPI on May 12: Headline 3.8% YoY (+0.6% MoM) — highest since May 2023; Core 2.8% YoY (+0.4% MoM — highest monthly core since Jan 2025). Energy +17.9% YoY; gasoline +28.4% YoY (Hormuz-linked). Food +3.2% YoY; shelter +3.3% YoY. Market reaction: S&P 500 down ~0.4%, Nasdaq down ~0.92%, CME FedWatch raises year-end rate HIKE probability to ~30%. Stagflation trap deepens as hot CPI confirms energy shock is broadening into services and shelter.

label: Washington DC — Warsh Fed Chair Confirmed (May 13); April PPI +6.0% YoY — Double Inflation Shock Week
sub: May 13: (1) Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve Chair — Powell era ends May 15; Warsh assumes responsibilities May 15; first FOMC June 9-10. (2) BLS released April 2026 PPI: +6.0% YoY (hottest since Dec 2022), +1.4% MoM (vs +0.5% estimate — 2.8x). Core PPI: +1.0% MoM (vs +0.4% estimate). Two-day inflation shock: CPI 3.8% (May 12) + PPI 6.0% (May 13). 10Y treasury yield: ~4.50-4.55% (up from 4.32% May 8). CME hike odds: ~30% by year-end. Warsh inherits: core PCE 3.2%, CPI 3.8%, PPI 6.0% — worst inflation inheritance since the Iran war began.

label: Frankfurt — ECB Hikes 25bp to 2.25%; First Hike Since July 2023
sub: June 11, 2026: ECB Governing Council raised all three key rates 25bp — deposit facility to 2.25%, main refi to 2.40%, marginal lending to 2.65% (effective June 17). New staff projections: HICP 3.0%/2.3%/2.0% (2026-28); growth cut to 0.8%/1.2%/1.5%. Lagarde cited Iran-war energy inflation and left the door open to further tightening.

label: Tokyo — BOJ Hikes to 1.00%, Highest Since 1995; Same Day as Warsh's First FOMC
sub: June 16, 2026: BOJ raised its overnight call rate 25bp to 1.00% (7-1 vote, Asada dissenting) — highest since 1995 — citing Iran-war energy pass-through. Landed same day as Warsh's first FOMC opened, reviving August-2024 carry-unwind fears. Nikkei +0.46%, yen ~160.22/USD on the day; yen later fell to a 40-year low (>162) by June 30 despite the hike.

label: Washington DC — Warsh's First FOMC Holds at 3.50–3.75%; Hawkish Dot Plot
sub: June 16-17, 2026: Warsh's inaugural FOMC unanimously held the fed funds rate at 3.50-3.75%. 2026 median dot rose to 3.8% from 3.4% in March — implying a hike, not a cut — with 9 of 18 members projecting ≥1 hike. Warsh declined to submit his own dot; statement cut to ~130 words from 341. Landed same day as the signed US-Iran MOU, which crashed Brent ~11% and partially offset the hawkish signal.

label: Beijing — China Q2 2026 GDP Grows 4.3%, Missing Forecast — Slowest in 3.5 Years
sub: July 14, 2026: China Q2 GDP +4.3% YoY (missed 4.5% forecast; down from 5.0% Q1) — slowest pace in ~3.5 years; +0.9% QoQ. H1 fixed-asset investment -5.7% YoY (real estate -18%). July 15 activity data mixed: industrial production +5.3% YoY beat, retail sales +1.0% YoY soft — fueling stimulus speculation ahead of the late-July Politburo meeting.

label: Washington DC — IMF July 2026 WEO: Global Growth 3.0%, Inflation Revised Up as Disinflation Stalls
sub: July 8, 2026: IMF's July WEO Update projected global growth of 3.0% (2026) and 3.4% (2027) — roughly unchanged cumulatively from April, but down from the 2024-25 average of 3.5%. Global headline inflation revised up to 4.7% as the IMF said disinflation had 'stalled.' Risks called 'more balanced than April' post-Iran-deal, but continued downside risk flagged from renewed conflict or repricing.

label: Washington DC — Section 122 Tariff Cliff 8 Days Out; No Congressional Action; Section 301 Timing in Doubt
sub: July 16, 2026: Section 122 tariff authority set to expire July 24 with no Congressional action reported (extension needs 60 Senate votes). USTR's Section 301 fallback (60 economies) closed its comment period July 6 and held its hearing July 7, but the required ≥30-day pre-effect notice period puts its readiness by July 24 in doubt — raising the prospect of a tariff-revenue coverage gap.
